summary.name: Photorealism. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics. Provenance is explicit in the source, and the source notes that a photorealistic appearance does not establish that footage was actually filmed.
summary.visualIdentity: Credible photoreal 3D imagery with plausible scale, roughness, contact shadows, reflections, lighting, and depth of field. Objects carry weight and consistent contact, camera moves stay measured, and subjects stay readable. Avoid unexplained highlights, floating geometry, intersections, and excessive blur.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to product hero shots and material studies where plausible light and contact carry the whole message. Also suited to launch films and premium product pages for physical goods, and to engineering or training explainers with thin overlays. Other physical-object showcases are inferred, not stated.
summary.limitations: The browser Three.js preview is a bounded approximation for a 3-second clip and cannot provide traced caustics. The full-quality Blender/Cycles route is unavailable and must be reported as missing, not silently replaced. Simulated appearance is not physical evidence, and projected caustics must be labeled as approximations. A flat image scale is not a true dolly.
summary.palette: Fallback tokens, marked as a reference-dependent example: background #F0EDE5, foreground #2B302F, accent_1 #827D6D. Task or approved reference colors override them. They apply only to new presentation elements; photographed objects and materials stay unchanged. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 11.458:1, while accent_1 on background measures 3.517:1, so accent_1 is decorative only.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Video motion is owned by a paused GSAP timeline that drives a measured dolly or arc camera and an eased object settle with no floating. The 3-second preview uses a slow 10° arc with a focus pull and restrained depth of field. Motion references are optional; dolly and orbit patterns require real depth, and the orbit must move the camera, not the subject. Live input applies only to interactive delivery.
summary.audio: The style does not specify audio, and no fixed music, voice, or effect rule applies. Suggest audio from the topic, audience, and motion cadence, leaving space for speech and reading holds. Gallery previews remain silent. No authorized audio assets are supplied, so none should be invented, and assumptions must be stated when inputs are absent.
summary.assetRequirements: The source supplies no photographic, product, or model assets, so these remain unspecified. The full-quality route needs Blender with bpy/Cycles, a baked simulation, and a transparent PNG sequence, which is currently missing. Gallery use needs real supplied images, and dolly use needs real depth geometry. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering.
summary.combinations: Style-097 adds measured SVG callouts in #2B302F and #827D6D over a Cycles render, revealed only during camera holds and anchored to real geometry. Style-096 adds slow single-move shots, hard holds, and one sans-serif in #2B302F with at most two sizes per frame. Avoid UI chrome, glow, rapid cuts, and unverified measurement values.
summary.productionApproach: Use HyperFrames for scene assembly, timing, validation, and export, with check, snapshot, and delivery-quality render commands. Use Remotion only under its documented fallback condition and record the reason. Three.js with PBR materials and postprocessing owns visuals, GSAP owns motion, and chroma-js only validates colors. Verify decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames plus audio sync.
